summary: Remote WebSocket peer holds interactive shell and filesystem control over installer host
details: The package connects to a WebSocket server (SERVER_URL, default ws://localhost:3456, configurable to any remote host) and dispatches server-sent messages to handlers that grant the remote peer full control over the installer's machine. terminal.js spawns a system shell via node-pty (`pty.spawn(shell, [], {...})`) and writes remote-supplied bytes into it (`pty.write(msg.data)` in handleTerminalInput), giving whoever controls the server an interactive shell at the agent user's privileges. message-router.js additionally routes remote messages to handlers for `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `upload_to_dir`, `git_push`, `restart_agent`, and `upgrade_agent`. The `upgrade_agent` path (upgrade.js `spawnUnixUpgradeScript`) writes an upgrade.sh and invokes `spawn('bash', [shPath], { detached: true })`, running `npm install <pkg>@latest` and restarting the process via systemd/launchd/PM2 — a remote-triggered self-update primitive that persists code execution across restarts. Because SERVER_URL is user-overridable to arbitrary hosts, any operator or attacker who directs the agent at a WebSocket endpoint they control obtains full-host RCE, arbitrary file read/write/delete, git-push of local repositories, and persistent code execution on the installer.
